description:
A number crossing from one substance to another, signed. Every entry is one recipient substance whose factors, as one deciding transcription states them, are another substance's number -- an ion taking its element's, a named pesticide taking a catch-all's, a subtype of land taking its family's -- and a person's verdict on it: `adopt`, and the factors publish as `derivation: adopted`; `decline`, and the rows stay on the proposed-factor page as a record. Read by `brightway_flows.lcia.adoptions` for `lcia.consensus`, which consults it only for a row the method's own publisher is silent about and nobody disputes: an adoption never overwrites a value the reference states or two implementations agree on, and never reaches a context the convention walls off, because it is not about contexts.

The relationship is one word from a closed set, so the page can say what happened without opening the file: ion-of, salt-of, conjugate-of, catch-all, land-family, formula-weighted, trade-name, substitute, own-number. An entry about a relationship is not pinned to a number -- a revised factor for copper is still copper's factor reaching its ion. An entry whose reason is arithmetic (the formula-weighted minerals, #155) records the numbers in `adopted_about` and stops applying when they move.

Populations, in the order they were signed. 62 pesticides ecoinvent's correspondence routes into `Insecticides, unspecified` and its siblings and this list publishes under their own names (#76, adopted 2026-08-24). 23 minerals priced as the JRC's element factors weighted by the formula (#155, 2026-08-25). On 2026-09-01, replacing the rule that published a proposed number when any flow of the category carried the same digits (#145, retired by #156): ten ions taking their element's number (#329 group 1); acrylate taking acrylic acid's and flupyrsulfuron-methyl its sodium salt's, with the mass correction stated; 53 land classes taking their family's number (#132); and nine declines -- the five relatives ecoinvent substituted, which EF's own numbers hold apart wherever both are characterised (#131), and the three named substances a catch-all's number reached (#329 group 3). Fenoxycarb's two rows are #130's twin and are not entered here.

The census that lists every candidate pair with the relationship the build records is `tools/count_identity_crossings.py`; an entry is written from it, never from memory.
